name: dynamic_stop_regime_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Fixed stop-losses are a primary source of unnecessary losses in intraday trading — too tight in volatile regimes (stopped out by noise before move materializes), too wide in calm regimes (give back too much profit when wrong). By dynamically setting stop-loss distance based on current volatility regime (ATR percentile), we optimize the probability of being stopped out by noise versus genuine reversal. Low-vol regime (ATR_Pctile < 30): stop = 1.0 * ATR(14). Medium-vol (30-70): stop = 1.5 * ATR(14). High-vol (>70): stop = 2.5 * ATR(14). The base signal is EMA(10)/EMA(25) crossover with VWAP confirmation. The inefficiency is that most traders use fixed bps stops that don't adapt to current conditions.

indicators.name: Vol_Regime
indicators.params: LOW if ATR_Pctile < 30; MED if 30-70; HIGH if > 70

indicators.name: Dynamic_Stop_Mult
indicators.params: 1.0 if Vol_Regime == LOW; 1.5 if MED; 2.5 if HIGH

conditions: Stop_Distance / close * 10000 < 60 bps (max allowable stop distance)

exit.stop_loss: Stop_Distance from entry (dynamically sized by regime)
exit.trailing_stop: After 1.0 * Stop_Distance profit, trail at 0.6 * Stop_Distance from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: EMA(close,10) crosses EMA(close,25) against position direction

risk.position_sizing: Risk-normalized: position = capital * max_risk / Stop_Distance. Size automatically shrinks in high-vol (wider stops)

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 28; if VIX > 24, use Dynamic_Stop_Mult = 3.0 (even wider stops)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 must be trending in same direction (EMA(NIFTY,10) vs EMA(NIFTY,25))
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day; widen stops by 50% on RBI policy day
other_filters: Stop_Distance must be at least 10 bps (avoid degenerate stops in ultra-low-vol periods)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — dynamic stop sizing is a risk management innovation that improves any base strategy; the edge is structural, not signal-dependent

weaknesses: In HIGH-vol regime, 2.5 * ATR(14) can be very wide (40-60 bps for volatile bank stocks), meaning each loss is large — even with smaller position size, this can hit daily loss limits quickly
The 120-bar lookback for ATR percentile means the strategy misses rapid volatility regime changes that occur within the first 2 hours (e.g., sudden news at 10:00 when percentile is still calibrating)
The 60 bps maximum stop constraint can filter out valid HIGH-vol setups in highly volatile names, reducing the universe during the most volatile (and potentially profitable) sessions
prior_art: ATR-based stops (Wilder, Van Tharp); Keltner Channel stop placement; volatility-scaled position sizing common in CTAs; regime-dependent stop multipliers less standardized
notes: The 1.8:1 reward-to-risk ratio is designed to be profitable at 50% win rate after costs (1.8 * 0.50 - 1.0 * 0.50 = 0.40, minus ~9 bps costs ≈ 31 bps edge). Consider using a continuous function for Stop_Mult instead of discrete regime buckets.
